observation.visible_scene: A dim, nighttime outdoor view dominated by a corrugated/ribbed metal fence or railing running diagonally across the lower two-thirds of the frame. Mounted at the top edge of this fence is a single intense white-blue light that produces a starburst lens flare and bright vertical streaks of reflected light running down the ribbed surface below it. Higher up and slightly to the left of the white-blue light, a small, steady yellow-orange light sits atop a thin post against the dark background. The overall scene is otherwise unlit and featureless.
visible_changes: The white-blue light and the small yellow light keep a fixed relative arrangement (yellow up and left of the bright light) throughout all frames, while the fence slats, the bright light and the yellow light all shift together across the image, indicating the motion is camera translation/pan rather than movement of the lights themselves.

The camera pans horizontally: the bright light drifts rightward in frame from the start (~x=535) to about the middle of the clip (~x=670-690 around frames 15-20), then drifts leftward again toward the end (~x=520 by frame 41).

Concurrently the camera tilts/drifts vertically so that the bright light moves gradually downward in the frame (from ~y=495 at the start to ~y=605 at the end), and the diagonal fence line flattens somewhat over time.

The white-blue light remains continuously on at roughly constant brightness and size; its starburst flare and the vertical reflection streaks on the fence persist without flicker, onset, or offset within the excerpt.
The small yellow light stays continuously on and unchanged in appearance.
No editing cut or discontinuity is visible; the sequence reads as one continuous handheld shot.
outside_clip_unknowns: The identity of the bright source (e.g. lamp, spotlight, or pointed flashlight) and of the yellow light is not determinable from these frames.
What lies beyond the fence or behind the lights, and whether the camera motion continues or reverses after the clip, is unseen.
The cause of the camera pan/tilt (a person walking, a handheld shake, or a deliberate sweep) is not shown.
uncertain_details: Whether any part of the apparent drift of the bright light is genuine object movement versus pure camera motion cannot be fully separated, though the consistent relative positions of all scene elements favor camera motion.
The exact material of the ribbed surface (metal fence, radiator-like panel, etc.) is inferred from the vertical streak pattern and is not certain.

trace.prompt:
Observe this actual video clip before reading any existing caption.
These are chronological samples of a TEMPORALLY CROPPED SEGMENT of a longer source video.
Both ends are arbitrary crop boundaries, not the beginning and completion of an action. Motion
may already be underway in the first view and may continue beyond the last. The endpoints need
NOT match or connect as a loop. Do not judge different endpoints as a physical inconsistency,
and do not invent a trigger, contact, start, stop, landing, disappearance or completion to make
the excerpt form a complete story. Missing context outside this segment stays unknown.
If an editing cut is visible inside the segment, distinguish it from continuous physical motion;
do not invent a smooth transition or a causal mechanism to connect the two views.
Describe what is visible during the excerpt, the actual changes, and supported persistent
properties. Cover the main visible process, not just scenery. Distinguish object movement from
camera movement, reflection from separate objects, expansion from translation, deformation from
occlusion, and an already ongoing process from its onset. Only state what the clip supports;
do not invent causes, an earlier impact, an unseen operator, material identities or later outcomes.
Do not infer motion from one frame, a visible seam or a single pose. Static intervals are valid.
Do not supply named physics laws. Compare each important entity's first and last image positions
and their relative positions before describing motion. Treat camera motion as uncertain when the
background evidence is insufficient, and retain clear relative changes despite that uncertainty.
Return JSON {"visible_scene":"...", "visible_changes":["observation supported within the excerpt"],
"outside_clip_unknowns":["unseen prerequisites or outcomes, only when relevant"],
"uncertain_details":["..."]}. Be concrete and concise, in English. This is not a complete event reconstruction.
